review_scope_note: Unlike prior API-based reviews that saw only the finding text, this audit had full repository access: experiment kernels, archived run logs/CSVs, prior reviews, remediations, and paper/CERTIFICATE.md where applicable. Quantitative claims were checked against primary artifacts; arithmetic and hashes were recomputed where feasible. No computational result was invented.
verification_methods: Read finding fully; compared every density/exception claim to scripts/experiments/zaremba-density/results/*.log and harvest_all.json / analysis_1e11.json
sha256sum of gpu_A123_1e10.log (225 bytes, no RESULTS) and cross-check against frontmatter checksum
Verified A12/A123/A124/A135/A2345 densities from RESULTS blocks; checked spectrum_n10.csv for Hausdorff values
Reviewed remediations and prior silver consensus against artifact gaps

claim_reviews.claim: A={1,2,3} has exactly 27 uncovered denominators at N=1e9, all <=6234.
claim_reviews.evidence: gpu_A123_1e9.log: Uncovered: 27, Covered: 999999973/1000000000; list matches page.

claim_reviews.claim: The same 27 exceptions persist through a completed N=1e10 run (density 99.9999997%).
claim_reviews.evidence: gpu_A123_1e10.log is 225 bytes with only a header and "Launching 531441 GPU threads..." — no RESULTS block. Its SHA-256 9b0a369a... matches the frontmatter checksum, so the finding cites a checksum of an incomplete log. harvest_all.json and HF_README list A123 only through 1e9.
claim_reviews.concerns: Do not claim completed 1e10 coverage until a RESULTS artifact exists.

claim_reviews.claim: Comparison table listing A={1,2} density 72.06% under a "d <= 1e10" header.
claim_reviews.evidence: 72.06% is the 1e9 value; at 1e10 the log shows 76.5486819100%. The table mixes scales.

claim_reviews.claim: A={2,3,4,5} densities ~97.29% (1e9), 97.14% (1e10), 98.78% (1e11) show non-monotone approach and refute δ>1/2 as a sharp sufficient density threshold.
claim_reviews.evidence: Matching RESULTS in A2345 logs; spectrum δ≈0.5596>1/2 while density remains below 100%. Framing is empirically sound and appropriately hedged.

claim_reviews.claim: Hausdorff dimension δ({1,3,5})=0.6240 in the finding table.
All 1023 nonempty subsets of {1..10} computed at 1e6; digit-1 dominance among near-100% sets.
claim_reviews.evidence: density_all_subsets_n10_1e6.csv has 1023 data rows; recomputed counts of high-density sets match the finding.

claim_reviews.claim: {1,2,6}=1834 and {1,2,7}=7178 are stable from 1e10 to 1e11; {1,2,8/9/10} still growing at 1e11.
claim_reviews.evidence: Confirmed in corresponding gpu_A126/127/128/129/1210_1e11 logs and analysis_1e11.json.
claim_reviews.concerns: Stability is observational within completed ranges, not a finiteness proof — page hedges this correctly for these sets.

missing_references: Completed RESULTS for A={1,2,3} at >=1e10 (or remove the completed-1e10 claim)
Correct δ({1,3,5}) citation from spectrum CSV (~0.58137)
Pin sha256_gpu_source to the current kernel or the commit that matched b07cd368…
overall_assessment: This remains one of the project's most valuable computational surveys: the 1023-subset sweep, the A2345 counterexample to naive δ>1/2 sufficiency, and the stable/open exception hierarchy at 1e11 are real and important. The silver consensus is too high while the flagship "27 exceptions through completed 1e10" claim is backed by a checksum of a partial log with no RESULTS block, and while the first density table mixes N-scales and misstates δ({1,3,5}).
recommendations: Either publish a completed A123@1e10 RESULTS block or rewrite claims to "verified through 1e9; 1e10 incomplete"
Relabel every density table cell with its N; fix δ({1,3,5})
Refresh HF_README and kernel SHA pinning
Keep the δ>1/2 counterexample framing — it is the scientific core
certification_justification: Core empirical patterns are strongly supported by logs, but a headline completion claim fails machine-check against its own cited artifact. Most-conservative certification should be bronze until the 1e10 A123 gap is closed.
